description: ediblecity is an R package developed at the Catalan Institute for Water Research to estimate city-scale benefits of urban agriculture. It constructs scenarios from spatial land-use objects and calculates food production, green-space access, heat-island measures, employment, volunteering, nitrogen-dioxide removal and rainfall runoff. The repository supplies example spatial data and adjustable parameters for gardens, vacant plots and rooftops. GitHub and CRAN provide the package, while Zenodo preserves the release cited by the software article. The package DESCRIPTION states MIT licensing, so reuse is free. The model uses user-supplied city information, not a fixed historical time series. Default coefficients have limitations and suitability rules need review before transfer to another city. It can compare green-infrastructure and food-production scenarios; no directly related catalogue record was identified.
